_comment: Every threshold the feature extractor uses. No defaults live in the code. Every key must have an entry in _provenance; extract_features.py refuses to run otherwise. Under the organisers' 2026-11-03 rules nothing may be tuned on the ground truth or the video: a value is either published, follows from the Laws of the Game or physics, or is an a-priori choice to be tuned on EXTERNAL data only (tuned_on names the dataset once that happens).

fps.source: games.py GAMES['BAR-ATH']['fps'] and DATA.md; the script asserts the two agree
fps.reason: Frame rate of the tactical video and its ATD.

kickoff_video_frames.reason: First-half kickoff is the first graded frame; second-half kickoff is 113742 (the 2nd half is graded from 110808, so 2,934 frames before it are dead ball).

kickoff_window_frames.source: IFAB Laws of the Game, Law 8 (The Start and Restart of Play)
kickoff_window_frames.reason: At a kickoff every player must be in their own half. Averaging positions over the 1 s (25 frames) before the kickoff reads each team's side robustly against single-frame tracking noise. Used only to find attacking direction.

kickoff_min_centroid_separation_m.source: IFAB Laws of the Game, Law 8
kickoff_min_centroid_separation_m.reason: With both teams in their own halves, their centroids are separated along the pitch length by a large margin. 5 m is a deliberately loose lower bound used only in an assertion, so a wrong axis orientation or kickoff frame makes the script stop instead of producing mirrored features. Not a modelling threshold.

ball_max_interp_gap_frames.reason: Linear interpolation assumes no touch inside the gap. Limiting it to 0.48 s (12 frames) keeps that assumption plausible while bridging short occlusions; longer gaps stay NaN so later stages can treat them as unknown.
ball_max_interp_gap_frames.revisit: tune on external matches with artificially dropped ball frames

velocity_half_window_frames.reason: Central difference over +/-2 frames (0.16 s total) balances noise against time resolution. Possession boundaries must be placed within a few frames, so wider windows would smear touches.

turn_min_speed_m_s.reason: Below about 1 m/s the ball's displacement over the velocity window (4 cm) is comparable to tracking jitter, so its direction is meaningless and the turn angle is set to NaN.
turn_min_speed_m_s.revisit: check against jitter measured on external tracking

ball_still_speed_m_s.source: IFAB Laws of the Game, Laws 8, 13, 14, 16, 17 (ball must be stationary at kickoffs, free kicks, penalties, goal kicks, corners)
ball_still_speed_m_s.reason: Restarts are taken from a stationary ball. 0.5 m/s is the 'stationary' cut-off, leaving room for tracking jitter.

ball_still_half_window_frames.reason: Stillness is measured over +/-0.48 s so a single slow frame in open play (a ball at the top of a bounce, a trap) does not look like a placed ball.

player_max_plausible_speed_m_s.source: human sprint record about 12.4 m/s (Bolt, 100 m, 2009); elite footballers top out around 10 m/s
player_max_plausible_speed_m_s.reason: A per-track velocity above any human's is a tracker identity switch, not running. Set just above the human record so no real sprint is dropped.

player_walking_speed_m_s.source: conventional football speed-zone boundary of 7.2 km/h between walking and jogging (e.g. Bradley et al. 2009, J Sports Sci)
player_walking_speed_m_s.reason: Share of players walking is a dead-ball cue: play stops and players slow down.

near_ball_radii_m.source: 3 m: design choice (about one stride plus reach); 10 m: IFAB Laws 8, 13, 17 require opponents at least 9.15 m from the ball at kickoffs, free kicks and corners
near_ball_radii_m.reason: Counts of players within playing distance (3 m) and within the restart exclusion distance (10 m, just above 9.15 m) of the ball.
near_ball_radii_m.revisit: 3 m radius: tune on external matches

smart_tagging_team_map.source: DATA.md Smart Tagging table: Team values are 'Barcelona', 'Atletic Club' (sic) and 'N/A'
smart_tagging_team_map.reason: Maps tag teams to the submission's H/A. N/A is kept as its own value (DATA.md: every throw-in is tagged N/A), never folded into a team.
